_comment: Soft-coded config for Equipment List extraction. Tune labels, patterns and Excel layout here — no Python changes needed.
_comment_async_backend: async_backend: 'celery' uses Celery broker (.delay) with automatic thread fallback when broker is unavailable; 'thread' always uses a background thread (no broker required — recommended for Railway where no Celery worker is deployed).

extraction._comment_tag: tag_pattern: captures PREFIX-NNN[-SUFFIX] where SUFFIX is an optional 1-4 char train/unit code (e.g. -TF, -1F, -2A). Without the suffix group, equipment sharing the same base number but different train codes (V-805-TF vs V-805-1F) are incorrectly collapsed into one row.
extraction._comment_tag_ignorecase: tag_pattern_ignorecase: compile tag_pattern with re.IGNORECASE so tags like C-010c-TF (OCR lowercase letter suffix) are still matched. The captured tag is always uppercased before use.
extraction._comment_slash_ocr: slash_ocr_substitutions: character pairs where the left char (OCR artefact) is replaced by the right char before slash-variant expansion runs. Common: OCR reads '/' as '?' in multi-unit pump tags like P-851A?B/C-TF.
extraction._comment_slash_collapse_space: slash_collapse_space_before_variant: when true, whitespace between BASE-NNN and the first variant letter is removed ONLY when the next pair is <letter>/<letter> (e.g. 'P-851 A/B/C-TF' → 'P-851A/B/C-TF'). Lets the slash-expansion regex find variant chains rendered with a space in title blocks. Set to false to disable.
extraction._comment_sibling_merge: merge_sibling_unit_variants: when true, equipment tags that share one data box but differ only by a single alpha variant letter (e.g. P-851A-TF, P-851B-TF, P-851C-TF) are merged into ONE row whose tag lists every variant joined by sibling_merge_separator (e.g. P-851A/B/C-TF) and whose 'quality_required' becomes the variant count. sibling_merge_min_group_size controls the minimum members required to trigger a merge (set to a high value like 99 to effectively disable without flipping the flag). This runs as an additive post-processing step — no core extraction logic is altered.
extraction._comment_spatial: spatial_word_y_bucket_pts: vertical band (points) used to group words onto the same line in the spatially-sorted word pass. Increase for drawings with densely packed rows; decrease to separate rows that sit close together.
extraction._comment_bond: span_bond_gap_pts: max horizontal gap (PDF points) between two adjacent span fragments to bond them into one token. CAD tools like SmartPlant/AVEVA split 'V-308-TF' into spans; bonding reconstructs the full tag. Increase if still split; decrease if unrelated tokens are being joined.
extraction._comment_ocr_thresh: min_vector_chars_for_ocr_skip: if extracted vector text is shorter than this, the OCR fallback is triggered. Set to a very high value (e.g. 99999999) to ALWAYS run OCR in addition to vector text.
extraction._comment_always_ocr: always_include_ocr: when true, OCR results are always appended to the text pool even when vector text exceeds the threshold. Useful for CAD P&IDs where tag text may be vector but rendered in a non-standard encoding.
extraction._comment_titleblock_rev: Title-block revision extraction for P&ID drawing mode. When _REVISION_USE_TOPMOST=True in Python, the document revision extracted from the title block is applied to ALL equipment items on the drawing. The three strategies (label, drawn-context, dwg-no proximity) are implemented in Python; only the enable flag is soft-coded here. Set titleblock_revision_enabled to false to disable and keep per-tag pre-text revision extraction.
extraction._comment_scale: ocr_render_scale: DPI multiplier for A4/small pages. 3.0 = ~216 dpi. For large-format A0/A1 P&IDs use ocr_render_scale_large_format — raise this if small tag text is missed.
extraction._comment_additional_scales: ocr_additional_scales_large_format: extra render scales to run on large-format pages IN ADDITION to ocr_render_scale_large_format. Results from all scales are pooled. Set to [] to disable — on multi-page A0/A1 P&IDs the extra pass is too slow and 2.0x alone gives good coverage.
extraction._comment_large_threshold: ocr_large_page_threshold_pts: pages whose smallest dimension exceeds this use the large-format render scale. A4 landscape min=595, A3=842, A1/A0>1000.
extraction._comment_ocr: ocr_rotation_angles: angles (degrees) to OCR each page at. 0=horizontal, 90=vertical (bottom-to-top). 180/270 rarely add value for equipment tags on P&IDs and double OCR time on large multi-page drawings.
extraction._comment_psm: ocr_psm_modes: Tesseract page-segmentation modes. 11=sparse text (best for scattered P&ID tags), 6=uniform block (tabular registers). Both run and results are merged.
extraction._comment_tile: Tile-based OCR splits A0/A1 pages into a grid before OCR. Each tile is smaller so Tesseract handles scattered text better. ocr_tile_rows/cols define the grid; set either to 0 to disable. Reduced to 2x2=4 tiles (from 3x4=12) so 28-page P&IDs complete within the 50-min Celery time limit.
extraction._comment_exclude_suffix: exclude_tag_suffixes: exact suffixes (after the hyphen) that identify NON-equipment tokens — e.g. project change-request numbers (PJ-2025-CR-002 OCR misread as P-2028-CR). Tags whose suffix matches any entry here are discarded.
extraction._comment_bare_flow_pat: flowrate_bare_value_pattern: bare unit scan for flow/volume units. MW and KW intentionally excluded — power units are handled by Strategy 3 (heat-exchanger only). Prevents kW motor annotations near vessels from polluting design_flowrate.
extraction._comment_flow_val_pat: flowrate_value_pattern: label-triggered flow value pattern. MW and KW removed; power duty for HX is handled by Strategy 3 in _extract_equipment_items.
extraction._comment_area: area_pattern: capture group 1 returns the code/number only (not the keyword). Add more keywords here as needed.
extraction._comment_area_heuristic: area_from_tag_heuristic: derive area code from serial number digits when no keyword found (V-101→100, P-2201→2200)
extraction._comment_area_ctx: area_context_chars: chars each side of tag to scan for area keyword (wider than ctx window to reach title blocks)
extraction._comment_desc_ctx: description_context_chars: wider post-tag window for newline-based description extraction
extraction._comment_desc_min: description_min_word_length: tokens shorter than this are skipped in description extraction
extraction._comment_desc_databox: description_databox_min/max_words: controls Strategy 0 (data-box title extraction). The first non-tag, non-pipe line after the equipment tag that has at least min_words purely alphabetic tokens is used as the description. max_words caps how many words are kept.
extraction._comment_nozzle: nozzle_pattern: nozzle tags N1/N-1/N1A. N[-]? covers both N1 and N-1 styles common on P&IDs
extraction._comment_nozzle_ctx: nozzle_context_chars: scanner radius (chars) each side of tag — wider catches nozzle schedules in separate table blocks
extraction._comment_material: material_class_pattern: covers O&G steel grades, piping spec codes, alloys, plastics and ASTM grades
extraction._comment_material_label: material_label_pattern: label-based extraction e.g. MATERIAL: CS, SHELL: SS316L, MTL: DUPLEX — capture group 1 is the value
extraction._comment_mat_ctx: material_context_chars: scanner radius for material code — 400 chars reaches most equipment data boxes
extraction._comment_service_label: service_label_pattern: label-based fluid extraction e.g. SERVICE: CRUDE OIL, FLUID: GAS — capture group 1 is the value
extraction._comment_service_ctx: service_context_chars: scanner radius for service/fluid — wider context reaches service labels on equipment bubbles
extraction._comment_notes: note_pattern: NOTE/SEE NOTE/HOLD/TBD/TBC/REF.DWG references adjacent to equipment
extraction._comment_process_params: Soft-coded patterns for process parameter extraction from P&ID data bubbles / annotation callouts near each equipment tag. process_param_context_chars controls how many chars each side of the tag are scanned. 400 chars is needed for detailed data boxes (e.g. Rejlers O&G P&IDs with 8+ fields listed after the tag).
extraction._comment_press: Pressure value pattern: capture group 1 = numeric value, group 2 = unit. Covers PSIG/PSIA/PSI, barg/bara, kPag, MPa.
extraction._comment_press_label: Label patterns that precede an operating or design pressure value in a data box.
extraction._comment_temp: Temperature value pattern: capture group 1 = numeric value. Matches °F / °C / DEG F / DEG C / DEGF / DEGC. A trailing negative-lookahead on [A-Z] prevents 'FAR', 'CARBON', etc.
extraction._comment_temp_label: Label patterns that precede an operating or design temperature value.
extraction._comment_dual_val: Slash-separated dual-value fields: 'LABEL (MIN/MAX) : V1/V2 UNIT' or 'LABEL : V1 / V2 UNIT'. Group 1=first value, group 2=second value, group 3=unit (optional for temp). Common on P&IDs where one data-box field stores both min and max condition.
extraction._comment_flow: Flowrate label + value. Group 1 = number, group 2 = unit. The label pattern also matches Q= and RATED Q= shorthand common on P&IDs.
extraction._comment_flow_val: Flowrate value pattern. Covers volumetric (m3/h, BBL/D, GPM), mass (KG/H, T/H), gas (MMSCFD, NM3/H, MSm3/d) and heat duty (kW, MW, MMBTU/H, MMkcal/H) units.
extraction._comment_flow_bare: flowrate_bare_value_pattern: unit-only scan (no label) — fallback when the label is absent. Captures standalone values with recognised flow units in the equipment context window.
extraction._comment_flow_ctx: flowrate_context_chars: wider scan window for flowrate vs the general 300-char process param window, since flow annotations on P&IDs may sit in connected line labels further from the symbol.
extraction._comment_insulation: Insulation code lookup in narrow context. Covers oil-field standard codes. Add project-specific codes to the list.
extraction._comment_dimension: Length/Height and Diameter/Width patterns for equipment sizing from data boxes. Group 1 = value (mm assumed unless unit captured). dimension_length_context_chars: scan radius each side of the tag; wider than the general 300-char process-param window because dimension data boxes on P&IDs are often in a separate table some distance from the equipment tag in OCR text order. dimension_value_window: maximum chars scanned after the label match to find the numeric value — 60 chars handles multi-word labels with colon spacing.
extraction._comment_motor: Motor rating extraction. Group 1 = kW value. Covers kW, KW, HP, BHP, KVA and also shorthand MR / M.R. common on O&G P&IDs. Includes ELEC MOTOR, ELECTRIC MOTOR and NAMEPLATE variants seen on Rejlers drawings.
extraction._comment_motor_bare: Bare motor-rating scan (no label): captures lone kW/HP values in the WIDE motor context window when the label is absent. Only applied inside the motor-specific context so false positives on flowrate numbers are avoided.
extraction._comment_motor_ctx: motor_rating_context_chars: scan radius (chars each side of tag) used ONLY for motor rating search. Wider than process_param_context_chars because motor callouts on P&IDs are attached to the motor symbol via a lead line that can be far from the equipment tag text.
extraction._comment_motor_na: motor_na_display_value: value written into motor_rating for non-rotating equipment (vessels, tanks, drums, etc.) when no kW value is found in context. Change to empty string to leave blank, or 'N/A' to revert to old behaviour.
extraction._comment_quality: Quality / inspection level codes near equipment tag. Group 1 is the quality designation.
extraction._comment_ai_gap_fill: AI gap-fill pass: uses OpenAI GPT-4o (primary) + Gemini Flash (fallback) to extract fields still empty after regex pass. Both providers are tried using MultiModelAIService. Set ai_gap_fill_enabled to false to disable. ai_gap_fill_fields controls which fields are attempted. ai_gap_fill_context_chars is the text window (chars each side of the tag) sent to the model.
extraction._comment_ai_authoritative: ai_authoritative_fields: fields where the AI result ALWAYS overrides the regex/OCR extraction — guarantees deterministic, consistent output across users regardless of OCR noise variation (temperature=0). Use ONLY for fields where AI is more reliable than fuzzy regex heuristics (e.g. equipment description, MOC). The AI is still called with min_empty=1 as long as description is listed in ai_gap_fill_fields; fields listed here are simply force-included in every AI call. Set to [] to disable the override and revert to regex-first behaviour.
extraction._comment_dim_reject_tag_serial: dimension_reject_tag_serial: when true (default), the equipment tag's numeric serial (e.g. 851 from P-851A-TF) is excluded from candidate dimension values. OCR on P&IDs commonly bonds the tag serial to a nearby 'MM' literal producing spurious lengths like '851 MM' or '803 MM'.
extraction._comment_quality_spec_in_remarks: quality_spec_in_remarks: when false (default), quality/NACE references are NOT written into the Remarks column. Oil & Gas equipment lists typically leave Remarks for project-specific notes; NACE applicability is derived from service fluid and drawing notes and is NOT a per-row property. Set to true to restore legacy behaviour.
extraction._comment_material_ocr_filter: material_reject_invalid_ocr: when true (default), MOC values that contain OCR-garbage keywords (HALF, OPEN, PIPE, CuNINoAN, LEVEL, NOTE, SHALL, SEE) or fail the [A-Z0-9 +/.-] token-shape test are rejected. AI gap-fill then provides a clean value. Set to false to keep raw regex output.
extraction._comment_connector_filter: Gate 1 — connector-arrow context check. On ADNOC/O&G P&IDs the sheet-edge continuation arrows have the format: '[KEYWORD] [DESCRIPTION] [TAG]\n[DWG-NO]'. If a flow-routing keyword (FROM/TO/VIA etc.) appears within connector_context_lookback_chars chars BEFORE a matched tag AND a cross-reference drawing number (4-5 hyphen-separated segments) appears within connector_context_lookahead_chars chars AFTER it, the tag is classified as a cross-sheet referenced item and skipped. Critically, it is NOT added to the deduplication set — so if the same tag appears later in its own data-box context on this sheet it will still be extracted correctly. Disable by setting connector_context_enabled to false.
extraction._comment_primary_filter: Gate 2 — data-box presence check. After the main extraction loop, any tag whose every process-parameter field is empty AND whose global databox index has no entry is discarded. This catches cross-sheet referenced equipment that escaped Gate 1 (e.g. references without an explicit drawing number on the same connector label). param_fields_for_primary_check lists the fields considered 'data-box indicators'. Disable by setting require_at_least_one_param to false.
extraction._comment_prefer_databox_index_filter: prefer_databox_index_filter: when true (default), Gate 2 uses the _databox_idx (proximity-based label:value scan) as the SOLE authoritative filter whenever it contains any entries. This is more reliable than the context-window param check because the databox scanner associates each value with the NEAREST preceding tag, making it immune to context-window bleed between closely-spaced equipment tags. Set to false to fall back to the older context-window param check in all cases.
extraction._comment_multi_page: multi_page_mode: 'per_page' (default) processes each PDF page as an independent P&ID drawing. Each page gets its own databox index, title-block DWG NO, and Gate 0/1/2 filtering — cross-page tag references cannot pollute other pages' results. 'combined' reverts to the old behavior where all pages are merged into one text blob before extraction.
extraction._comment_ctx_reject: Gate 0 — tag_context_reject_patterns: list of regex patterns checked against 80 chars around each matched equipment tag. If any pattern matches, the tag occurrence is skipped (NOT added to seen) — so the same tag can still be extracted from a legitimate data-box context elsewhere on the same page. Designed to exclude tags that appear inside revision-cloud annotations or other non-equipment callouts.
extraction._comment_desc_reject: description_reject_patterns: matched against the extracted description field — removes rows whose description is a known annotation label, not a real equipment name. Only add patterns for text that is NEVER a real equipment description (e.g. 'Revision Cloud'). Do NOT add vessel/equipment names here.
extraction._comment_desc_clear: description_clear_patterns: descriptions matching ANY pattern are BLANKED (not dropped) so the AI gap-fill pass re-extracts the correct data-box title. Use for known notes-bleed / fragment captures that are clearly not an equipment title: single generic words (Pump, Vessel), obvious notes sentences, datasheet fragments, or extraction artefacts. Only adds cleanup — never removes rows.
extraction._comment_dedup_desc: dedup_by_description_enabled: when true, items sharing the same description are deduplicated — the most-populated record is kept, OCR-variant duplicates are discarded.
extraction._comment_uppercase_fields: uppercase_fields: canonical uppercase is enforced on these fields at post-processing time. Material codes and abbreviations must render in capitals (e.g. 'cs' → 'CS', 'cS + LINING' → 'CS + LINING'). Applied after both regex extraction and AI gap-fill. Add a field key here to normalize its casing.

_comment_fluid_map: line_fluid_code_map: maps 1-4 char fluid/service codes from line designations to human-readable service names. Add project-specific codes here.
_comment_pipe_class: pipe_class_prefix_map: maps first 2 digits of a pipe class / spec code to a material hint. Calibrate per project spec book.
_comment_register: equip_register_fields: maps each 18-field key to a list of column header aliases found in Equipment Register CAD documents. Add project-specific abbreviations to any list without touching Python code.
_comment_register_note: Header variants are normalised (uppercase, & . - / stripped to spaces) before matching. You only need to cover the stripped form once — e.g. 'p id no' covers both 'P&ID No.' and 'P & ID No.' after normalisation.
_comment_register_threshold: equip_register_min_columns: min matched column headers required to treat doc as a register table (vs P&ID drawing)
_comment_register_rows: equip_register_min_rows: min data rows with ≥ 5 populated fields to accept register-mode results
_comment_register_skip: equip_register_skip_if_page_dim_gt: if the smallest page dimension (pts) exceeds this value, skip register mode entirely — large-format drawings (A1/A0 P&IDs) are never equipment registers. A4 = 595 pts, A3 = 842 pts, A1 = 1190 pts.
_comment_databox: databox_label_map: maps equipment data-box label variants (as they appear in CAD P&ID data boxes) to field keys. A list value [field_a, field_b] splits the raw value on '/' — first part→field_a, second→field_b — for MIN/MAX pairs. Put more-specific variants (with MIN/MAX qualifier) BEFORE shorter variants so first-match-wins applies correctly. databox_scan_window_chars: chars to look back from the label match to find the nearest equipment tag.
_comment_designation_codes: designation_codes: IEC/Linde/Borouge P&ID designation code table extracted from legend sheets. Maps 2-char designation code → human-readable type name and engineering category. This drives equipment type classification during extraction and populates the PIDEquipmentType database table. Add project-specific codes here — no Python changes needed.
_comment_tag_prefix_type: tag_prefix_type_map: maps the leading alphabetic portion of an equipment tag (e.g. 'V', 'P', 'E') to a designation code from designation_codes. Longer prefixes are checked first (ST before S). Used to auto-classify extracted tags by type. Add project-specific mappings here.
